Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll begin with the workspace contract in `README.md`, then use the required wake-visual and fish-control skills before touching the policy. I’ll trace the assigned parent, inherited logs, and sampled solver evidence so the single candidate and reusable lesson are both tied to observed outcomes.

The inherited guidance is already late-stage: displacement-only half-cycle steering plus the one-sided response-release gate is the capture-preserving baseline; velocity phase prediction, gate removal, raw velocity residuals, and pointwise rate tapers are evidenced failures. I’m now locating the exact parent and rollout artifacts, then I’ll inspect both visual rows for a strong capture and the most informative available failure before choosing a genuinely new mechanism.

The visual-signal skill confirms all four sampled rollouts satisfy direct-uniform still water and remain self-propelled: both sheets show a coherent alternating top-down street and compact three-dimensional caudal structures through capture. The key comparison is that three baseline/response-coupled variants are statistically alike (18.65–18.68 T, mean distance 2.0934–2.0940 L), while the terminal velocity/approach compound is slower (19.052 T, 2.09874 L) with essentially unchanged acceleration and rate contact. I’m now consulting the bookshelf as required; any transfer will be limited to one normalized feedback invariant.

The shelf supports one mechanism that fits the evidence without revisiting failed velocity steering: closed-loop CPG rate modulation. I’ll keep the captured displacement-only steering carrier unchanged and add a slow body-frame geometry schedule to the oscillator’s natural rate. Because every `ω`-dependent term—including the posterior `q̇₁/ω` lag normalization—is changed together, the dimensionless traveling-wave shape is preserved; this differs from the failed pointwise rate barriers that distorted individual half-cycles. The test is whether it retains capture and the ~2.093–2.094 L route band while reducing rate/acceleration contact; otherwise later workers should reject this frequency-scheduling branch.

The single candidate now adds only the geometry-conditioned oscillator-rate mechanism, with its parameter declared in `target_policy_params()`. The inherited route sign, displacement half-cycle scaling, response-release gate, amplitude schedule, posterior lag form, and hard acceleration projection are otherwise unchanged. I’m moving into static/contract validation now; I will not run CFD.

The workspace’s required checker is defined as a dedicated validation agent, so I’m invoking it now exactly as requested. It will run the guidance-difference check, lightweight Julia policy contract, and editable-boundary check—no CFD.

The required checker found one workspace-metadata defect and one environment limitation. The boundary check passed. The guidance checker cannot identify the assigned parent because `README.md` marks the same optimizer as “copied to guidance” twice; I’m inspecting that rendered duplicate and will make the minimal metadata repair, then rerun the checker. Julia is absent from this execution environment, so I’ll also use the repository’s static/schema checks and report that runtime limitation precisely.

After the metadata repair, the required checker now passes both the semantic guidance check and editable-boundary check. Its Julia command still cannot start because no `julia` executable or Julia module is exposed here; the checker classified that as an environment limitation, not a policy failure. I’m doing one final availability search plus static contract/diff audit so the handoff distinguishes verified properties from the one unexecutable runtime check.

Produced exactly one candidate: [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1).

It adds normalized target-lateral oscillator-rate scheduling while preserving the captured steering carrier and dimensionless posterior phase relationship.

Also updated:

- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) with visual diagnosis, evidence, bookshelf transfer block, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:106) with the reusable positive geometry-scheduling lesson and terminal-compound negative boundary.

Validation:

- Guidance semantic check: PASS
- Editable-boundary check: PASS
- Parameter-schema guard: PASS
- Julia runtime contract: not executable because `julia` is unavailable in the environment
- CFD was not run, per workspace instructions.
